perspective:
Keith’s available information:

- He is Keith Ndiaye, a construction worker; Elizabeth Sun is the receptionist at the same construction company. They are friendly, professional colleagues who interact during his office visits for paperwork/project updates.
- Recently, Keith observed Elizabeth being unusually curt with him over several days. He suspected he might have unknowingly upset her through a misunderstanding or mistake.
- He asked Elizabeth if he had done something to upset her. He heard her say no, not at all, that she was dealing with personal stuff, and that she was sorry if she seemed short.
- Keith felt sympathetic after learning her shortness was not anger toward him but personal stress. He offered to listen if she needed someone to talk to and suggested a coffee break. He heard her accept, call it kind, and thank him.
- During the coffee break, Keith heard Elizabeth share more about her stresses and formed the impression they were serious. He suggested talking to a professional, noting that an external perspective sometimes helps. He heard her say she had thought about it but was unsure and hesitant about seeking help.
- Afterward, Keith noticed Elizabeth became slightly withdrawn. He believed his suggestion about professional help might have embarrassed her or overstepped, and he felt regretful.
- He told Elizabeth he hoped he hadn’t overstepped and that he was there to support her no matter what. He heard her say he didn’t overstep, she appreciated his concern, and it was just a lot to think about.
- Later, Keith observed Elizabeth seeming more open and appreciative of his concern. He told her he was glad they talked and that he was always available to chat or take a break together. He heard her thank him, say it meant a lot, and that she felt better knowing she had his support.
- Keith believes Elizabeth values his support and feels more comfortable around him now. He intends to maintain this supportive relationship.
